title: Voters Reject ALPRs and Surveillance Tech at the Ballot Box

articleBody:
Do automated license plate readers (ALPRs) have any place in our communities? That question has been a hot topic in city council meetings, community conversations, and news coverage around the country for months. This past election day, a couple U.S communities took it further: to the ballot.

And overwhelmingly, voters decided that, no, these devices should not be deployed on our streets. We agree!

In Maine, the coastal community of York voted to remove the town’s existing ALPR cameras and require that any future proposed installations receive voter approval before proceeding. The local initiative ended up on the ballot after constituents gathered enough signatures on a citizens’ petition for a local ordinance. On Election Day, nearly three-quarters of York voters supported the ban.

Thousands of miles away, voters in League City, Texas also voted against allowing the local police department to continue use of ALPR cameras. That vote was formally approved on November 17, which began a 72-hour window to remove the cameras. Since the election, the cameras have been “bagged” or covered to prevent the collection of data.

At least one city also decided to expand protections afforded to their residents when it comes to the use of surveillance technology. In Pflugerville, Texas, Proposition B passed, now requiring that the City Charter be amended to include “protections governing the collection, use, retention, and oversight of data, facial recognition, and surveillance technologies.” It also requires “a responsible artificial intelligence framework.”

While every municipality has different rules for how to get a local ordinance placed on the ballot, banning use and securing the removal of surveillance tools locally is a powerful way of protecting your community against devices and data collection that goes far beyond your town lines.

Surveillance is a choice, not a mandate, and our communities have the power to refuse it. EFF has supported local communities around the country over the last few years in advocating against the procurement of surveillance technologies in their cities, counties, and states. These victories at the ballot box and in city councils show that when mass surveillance is presented as a policy choice, not a technical necessity, communities can and do reject it.

Do you know what surveillance tools are being used by your local police departments? Check out the Atlas of Surveillance to learn more about the tools in your city, and sign up to volunteer if you want to push for more transparency across the country.

title: Repräsentative Umfrage zeigt, wie Lehrkräfte zur Arbeitszeiterfassung stehen
subtitle: 55 Prozent der Lehrkräfte befürworten eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung, 34 Prozent sind dagegen.
feedText: Die übrigen 11 Prozent sind unentschlossen. Das zeigt eine repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage für das Deutsche Schulportal. Was versprechen sich Lehrkräfte von der Arbeitszeiterfassung, und welche Bedenken haben sie? Die Ergebnisse machen sichtbar, wie unterschiedlich die Erwartungen sind, während ein Bundesland bereits den Pilotversuch gestartet hat.
articleBody:
# Repräsentative Umfrage: Das sagen Lehrer zur Arbeitszeiterfassung

Seit den Urteilen des Europäischen Gerichtshofs und des Bundesarbeitsgerichts ist gerichtlich bestätigt, dass eine Arbeitszeiterfassung zum Gesundheitsschutz vorgeschrieben ist. Wird sie bald auch für Lehrkräfte eingeführt? © Getty Was für die meisten Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer in Deutschland eine Selbstverständlichkeit ist, gilt für Lehrkräfte als umstritten. Seit einem Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs aus dem Jahr 2019 und einer Entscheidung des Bundesarbeitsgerichts aus dem Jahr 2022 ist auch gerichtlich bestätigt, dass die Erfassung der gesamten tatsächlichen Arbeitszeit zum Gesundheitsschutz zwingend vorgeschrieben ist. Die KMK pochte auf eine Sonderregelung für Schulen, das Bundesarbeitsministerium bekräftigte, dass es keine Ausnahmen für den Schulbereich geben würde. Wie stehen aber die Lehrkräfte selbst zu einer verpflichtenden Erfassung ihrer Arbeitszeit?

Neue Daten, die dem Deutschen Schulportal exklusiv vorliegen, zeigen nun erstmals, dass eine Mehrheit der Lehrkräfte in Deutschland die Einführung einer verpflichtenden Arbeitszeiterfassung befürwortet. 55 Prozent sind dafür, 34 Prozent dagegen. Weitere 11 Prozent sind bei dem Thema noch unentschlossen. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine Umfrage, die das Meinungsforschungsinstitut Forsa im Auftrag der Robert Bosch Stiftung für das Deutsche Schulportal durchgeführt hat. Im September 2026 wurden insgesamt 1.056 Lehrkräfte an allgemeinbildenden und berufsbildenden Schulen in ganz Deutschland befragt. Die statistische Fehlermarge für die gesamte Lehrerschaft beträgt bis zu drei Prozentpunkte.

© Henriette Anders Infografik herunterladen Eine Zustimmung zur Arbeitszeiterfassung gibt es in fast allen befragten Gruppen. Besonders hoch ist sie bei Lehrkräften an Gymnasien, von denen 60 Prozent eine verpflichtende Erfassung befürworten. An Haupt-, Real- und Gesamtschulen liegt der Wert bei 56 Prozent, an Grundschulen bei 51 Prozent und an beruflichen Schulen bei 49 Prozent. Auch unter Schulleitungen und stellvertretenden Schulleitungen befürwortet eine Mehrheit die Arbeitszeiterfassung: 56 Prozent sind dafür, 35 Prozent lehnen sie ab.

## Warum viele Lehrkräfte eine Erfassung ihrer Arbeitszeiten wünschen

Doch was erhoffen sich Lehrkräfte von der Arbeitszeiterfassung? Die mit Abstand häufigste Antwort auf die offen gestellte Frage lautet: mehr Transparenz über die tatsächliche Arbeitsbelastung. Unter den Befürworterinnen und Befürwortern nennen 70 Prozent die Sichtbarmachung ihrer Arbeitszeiten und ihrer Arbeitsbelastung als wichtigstes Argument für die Einführung einer verpflichtenden Erfassung.

23 Prozent der Befürworterinnen und der Befürworter hoffen auf mehr Gerechtigkeit und Vergleichbarkeit zwischen Lehrkräften und Fächern. Weitere 15 Prozent nennen den Gesundheitsschutz und die Prävention von Überlastung, während 14 Prozent eine angemessene Vergütung oder Entschädigung für Überstunden als wichtigsten Grund anführen. 9 Prozent hoffen, dass die Erfassung der Arbeitszeiten dazu beiträgt, gesellschaftlichen Vorurteilen gegenüber dem Lehrerberuf entgegenzuwirken. Die Gründe für die Befürwortung oder die Ablehnung einer verpflichtenden Arbeitszeiterfassung wurden ohne vorgegebene Antwortoptionen anhand offener Fragen erhoben, wobei Mehrfachnennungen zulässig waren.

> Seit ich meine Arbeitsbelastung in der App erfasse, plane ich meine Woche deutlich bewusster.

Der Bremer Lehrer Björn Wolf erlebt bereits, wie die Arbeitszeiterfassung den Schulalltag verändern kann. Bremen ist in diesem Schuljahr als erstes Bundesland mit einem Pilotprojekt zur Arbeitszeiterfassung an Schulen gestartet. Wolf unterrichtet an der Oberschule an der Lerchenstraße, einer der teilnehmenden Schulen.

Auf der Fachtagung „Lehrkräftearbeitszeit als Hebel für gute Schule” am 4. November 2026 in Bremen schilderte er seine Erfahrungen: „Seit ich meine Arbeitsbelastung in der App erfasse, plane ich meine Woche deutlich bewusster“, berichtet Wolf. „Ich sehe, wie viele Stunden mir zur Verfügung stehen, und kann dann gezielt entscheiden: An welchen Tagen habe ich Unterricht? Wann bleibt Zeit zum Vorbereiten? Und wann passen die übrigen Aufgaben hinein?“ Die Tagung wurde vom Senator für Kinder und Bildung der Freien Hansestadt Bremen, der Telekom Stiftung, die das Bremer Pilotprojekt fachlich begleitet , der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Bildungsverwaltung und dem Netzwerk Schulentwicklung veranstaltet.

Auch der Leiter der Oberschule an der Lerchenstraße, Jonathan Dauber, sieht Chancen für einen besseren Arbeitsschutz. Vor allem jüngere Lehrkräfte an seiner Schule seien oft ständig erreichbar und täten sich schwer, Grenzen zwischen Arbeit und Privatleben zu ziehen. „Die Arbeitszeiterfassung kann helfen, ohne schlechtes Gewissen zu sagen: Jetzt bin ich nicht erreichbar.“

## Jede dritte Lehrkraft lehnt eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung ab

Dennoch stößt die verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung auch auf erheblichen Widerstand. Laut der Umfrage lehnen 34 Prozent der Lehrkräfte sie ab. Ihr häufigstes Argument ist, dass sich die tatsächlichen Arbeitszeiten im Lehrerberuf nur schwer zuverlässig erfassen lassen.

Unter den Gegnerinnen und Gegnern geben 40 Prozent als wichtigsten Grund an, dass die Arbeitszeiten von Lehrkräften praktisch nicht erfassbar, messbar oder kontrollierbar seien. Weitere 23 Prozent befürchten bürokratischen Mehraufwand, während 21 Prozent Bedenken haben, an Flexibilität einzubüßen oder eine Atmosphäre wachsenden Misstrauens zu schaffen. Seltener genannt werden die Vermischung von Privat- und Berufsleben (11 Prozent), Zweifel am grundsätzlichen Nutzen (8 Prozent) und die Gefahr eines Missbrauchs (7 Prozent).

Bedenken gegenüber der Arbeitszeiterfassung wurden auch auf der Fachtagung in Bremen deutlich. Sven Räther, stellvertretender Schulleiter des Hamburger Gymnasiums Ohmoor, stellte infrage, ob eine minutengenaue Erfassung mit den Realitäten des Lehrberufs vereinbar ist. „In der Theorie klingt das gut“, so Räther. „Aber eine Lehrkraft kann nicht sagen: ‚Die Arbeitszeit ist jetzt vorbei, lieber Schüler, ich habe keine Zeit mehr für dich.‘ Das ist entscheidend, denn genau dieser Teil macht unseren Beruf so besonders.“

Auch Jan Riedel, Bildungsminister des Landes Sachsen-Anhalt, äußert sich auf der Konferenz skeptisch. Er argumentierte, der Debatte fehle ein klar definiertes Ziel. Gehe es darum, die Schulen zu verbessern, eine gerechtere Verteilung der Arbeitsbelastung zu erreichen oder eine übermäßige Arbeitsbelastung sichtbar zu machen? „Ich befürchte, dass wir Erwartungen wecken, aber nicht klar definieren, was unser eigentliches Ziel ist“, sagt er.

## Bremen erprobt als erstes Bundesland die Arbeitszeiterfassung

Seit August 2026 erfassen in Bremen und Bremerhaven rund 700 Beschäftigte an neun Schulen ihre Arbeitszeiten digital mithilfe der App „Untis Arbeitszeit“. Erste Erkenntnisse deuten darauf hin, dass der Zeitaufwand für die einzelnen Einträge relativ gering ist. Laut Projektkoordinator an der Bremer Schulbehörde Kolja Buß sind 50 Prozent der Einträge innerhalb von 32 Sekunden erledigt, während 90 Prozent nicht länger als 82 Sekunden dauern. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt des Pilotprojektes liegt auf dem Arbeitsschutz. Untersucht wird zudem, wie gesetzliche Ruhezeiten im Schulalltag eingehalten werden können.

Dies kann insbesondere für Lehrkräfte mit kleinen Kindern eine Herausforderung darstellen, die möglicherweise erst spät am Abend Zeit finden, Unterricht vorzubereiten oder Aufgaben zu benoten. „Die Einhaltung der elfstündigen Ruhezeit ist ein Thema, das uns aus den Schulen bisher am häufigsten zurückgemeldet wurde“, berichtet Buß auf der Fachtagung.

## Rackles: Arbeitszeiterfassung könnte zu einer gerechteren Aufgabenverteilung führen

Für den Bremer Bildungssenator Mark Rackles (SPD) stellt die Einführung der Arbeitszeiterfassung einen großen kulturellen Wandel dar. In einem Interview mit dem Deutschen Schulportal im Juli 2026 erklärte er, dass Lehrkräfte bisher nur einen Teil ihrer Arbeitszeit nachweisen mussten. Künftig werde viel transparenter werden, wer wie viele Stunden arbeite.

Er erwartet, dass das System erhebliche Unterschiede in der Arbeitsbelastung zwischen einzelnen Lehrkräften aufzeigen wird. Dies könnte auch unangenehme Konsequenzen haben. Während Lehrkräfte mit besonders hoher Arbeitsbelastung Entlastung benötigen würden, könnte von anderen erwartet werden, zusätzliche Aufgaben zu übernehmen. „Die, die unterhalb des Arbeitssolls sind, müssen mehr arbeiten – das ist völlig klar“, so Rackles im Interview. Das würde jedoch nicht unbedingt mehr Unterrichtsstunden bedeuten. Stattdessen könnten zusätzliche Aufgaben gerechter auf das Kollegium verteilt werden.

## Was geschieht, sobald die Arbeitszeiten erfasst sind?

Doch selbst wenn eine Arbeitszeiterfassung eingeführt wird, bleibt eine entscheidende Frage offen: Was geschieht mit den gesammelten Daten? Rackles sieht die Chance, mit Hilfe der Daten, Aufgaben innerhalb der Schulen gerechter zu verteilen und übermäßige Arbeitsbelastungen abzubauen. Gleichzeitig könnten sie eine Grundlage dafür bieten, zusätzlichen Personalbedarf zu ermitteln und zu begründen.

Auf der Konferenz in Bremen betonte er, dass zusätzliche Mittel in Zeiten knapper öffentlicher Haushalte sorgfältig begründet werden müssen: „Mehr Ressourcen für Bildung geht immer“, sagt Rackles. „In der heutigen Zeit muss man aber sehr präzise sagen, wofür wir mehr Ressourcen brauchen. Wir brauchen konkrete Zahlen statt eines Bauchgefühls. Dieser Debatte muss man sich 2027 stellen.“ Ob eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung tatsächlich zur Entlastung der Lehrkräfte führt, wird daher weitgehend davon abhängen, wie Schulen und Bildungsbehörden die erhobenen Daten nutzen.

Die repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage macht erstmals deutlich, dass eine Mehrheit der Lehrkräfte eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung grundsätzlich befürwortet.

Mitarbeit: Jasmin Shamsi

Rackles sieht die Chance, mit Hilfe der Daten, Aufgaben innerhalb der Schulen gerechter zu verteilen und übermäßige Arbeitsbelastungen abzubauen. Gleichzeitig könnten sie eine Grundlage dafür bieten, zusätzlichen Personalbedarf zu ermitteln und zu begründen.

Auf der Konferenz in Bremen betonte er, dass zusätzliche Mittel in Zeiten knapper öffentlicher Haushalte sorgfältig begründet werden müssen: „Mehr Ressourcen für Bildung geht immer“, sagt Rackles. „In der heutigen Zeit muss man aber sehr präzise sagen, wofür wir mehr Ressourcen brauchen. Wir brauchen konkrete Zahlen statt eines Bauchgefühls. Dieser Debatte muss man sich 2027 stellen.“ Ob eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung tatsächlich zur Entlastung der Lehrkräfte führt, wird daher weitgehend davon abhängen, wie Schulen und Bildungsbehörden die erhobenen Daten nutzen.

Die repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage macht erstmals deutlich, dass eine Mehrheit der Lehrkräfte eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung grundsätzlich befürwortet.

Hilma af Klint, “Ser III No. 5” (1920) (image via [Bukowskis](https://www.bukowskis.com/en/news/for-the-first-time-in-three-decades-an-abstract-work-by-hilma-af-klint-at-auction?ref=hyperallergic.com) )

*Welcome to our roundup of daily art news, featuring top stories and timely updates handpicked by Hyperallergic's writers and editors. Have a news tip?* [Get in touch with us](https://hyperallergic.com/contact/) *.*

### Hilma af Klint Work Heads to Auction

Works by the Swedish spiritualist and abstract art pioneer, who asked that her paintings remain unseen for 20 years after her death in 1944, have not come up for auction in more than three decades. That's about to change with the emergence of “[Ser III No. 5](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/15/nx-s1-6034594/auction-of-rare-hilma-af-klint-artwork-illuminates-tensions-over-her-legacy?ref=hyperallergic.com)” (1920) at the Stockholm-based house [Bukowskis](https://www.bukowskis.com/en/news/for-the-first-time-in-three-decades-an-abstract-work-by-hilma-af-klint-at-auction?ref=hyperallergic.com), which estimates the oil and graphite on canvas will fetch up to 8 million SEK (~$791,000) in its upcoming November 18–19 sale. Controversy has [long followed the legacy of the late artist](https://hyperallergic.com/could-hilma-af-klint-works-be-removed-from-public-view/), with some arguing that her works should be kept together rather than sold and [commercialized](https://hyperallergic.com/relative-of-hilma-af-klint-condemns-nfts-of-artists-paintings/).

### Sotheby's Settles Dispute With Heirs Who Contested Van Gogh Sale

After the heirs of the Jewish publisher Samuel Fischer [requested the withdrawal of Van Gogh's “Châtaigniers en fleurs”](https://hyperallergic.com/restitution-claim-on-180m-van-gogh-shakes-up-sothebys-marquee-week/) (1890) from a sale at Sotheby's, claiming that the work had been sold under duress amid Nazi persecution in Europe, the family has reached a “mutually satisfactory resolution” with the work's consignors, said a Sotheby's statement shared with *Hyperallergic.* But will the dispute put a damper on sale results? We'll find out tonight when the painting, valued at $180 million, goes under the hammer.

title: ‘The Predators Are Real’: Senate Hearing Slams Roblox Over Child Sex Abuse
subtitle: US Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin have introduced legislation to make it easier for families to sue if their child has been harmed through the massive gaming platform.
feedText: US Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin have introduced legislation to make it easier for families to sue if their child has been harmed through the massive gaming platform.
articleBody:
# ‘The Predators Are Real’: Senate Hearing Slams Roblox Over Child Sex Abuse

People who say they were groomed on Roblox testified in front of a Congressional subcommittee Tuesday about safety risks associated with the popular gaming platform frequented by kids and teenagers.

“Roblox is one of the most popular gaming platforms in the world,” Republican senator Josh Hawley said in his opening remarks. “If your children are on Roblox they are being exposed in all likelihood to sexual predators … to sexually exploitative content, left, right, and center.”

The hearing was intended to address the bipartisan legislation introduced by Hawley and Democratic senator Dick Durbin, coauthors of the No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act, which would allow families of victims to sue Roblox directly instead of being forced to settle their claims privately in arbitration, as the platform’s terms of service currently dictate.

The process of forced arbitration “strips consumers and workers of their rights,” testified Myriam Gilles, a law professor at Northwestern University who is an expert on forced arbitration. “I never expected to come before this body to talk about its use against 9-year-olds, but that’s where we are.”

Roblox is currently facing nearly 200 lawsuits from families who allege that their children were groomed by sexual predators posing as children on the platform. According to Hawley, Roblox CEO David Baszucki was invited to testify at the hearing but declined.

“He may think he’s silent, but in fact he’s testifying, and what he’s testifying to is his commitment to money over people,” Hawley said.

In a statement, Sara Kanawati Stephany, a senior manager for US policy communications at Roblox, told WIRED, “Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat. A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety. Protecting children online takes stronger protections, better tools, and consistent standards that apply everywhere kids spend time online.”

Roblox has previously argued that users waive their right to sue in open court in the platform’s terms of agreement. According to Roblox’s own data , 35 percent of its age-checked daily active users are under the age of 13—too young to fully comprehend the terms of the agreement, witnesses argued.

“There is no way an 8-year-old could read those terms and then sign away their right to a moment in court, effectively silencing themselves,” Republican senator Katie Britt said after being presented with a copy of the multi-page agreement.

Two of those who testified before Congress were alleged survivors of grooming on the platform. One was Michael Schlep , a content creator who has advocated for more stringent child safety measures on the platform.

Schlep testified that when he was 12, he met a game developer on the platform who befriended him in a public chatroom, then moved to private chats. He alleges he was exposed to “violent pornography, cartel beheadings, and extreme racist ideologies” that he says was a result of his communication with this adult man, and that his abuser exposed his private information, leading to a suicide attempt. He currently runs a YouTube channel exposing alleged Roblox child predators and criticizing the platform for failing to protect children, which has led to Roblox hitting him with a cease-and-desist.

“Roblox must be held accountable publicly,” Schlep testified. “They will not voluntarily act to protect children.”

The hearing also featured testimony from a Marine Corps veteran identified as Woody Doe, who alleged that he was groomed, then sexually assaulted by an adult man he met on Roblox when he was 11 years old. “For years, I carried the shame of what happened,” he testified. He now has a lawsuit pending against Roblox for allegedly failing to warn parents and children of the dangers of the platform.

“I cannot go back and protect the 11-year-old boy I once was, but I can speak for him today … and prevent any other children from ever experiencing the same pain,” he said.

Roblox is a massive gaming platform, with about 138 million daily active users according to recent company data . As of 2025, 39.7 million daily active users were under the age of 13.

In response to the litigation and to intense media scrutiny, Roblox has adopted what it says are more stringent child-safety measures, including AI-assisted face recognition to estimate a user’s age. But Khari James, senior legal counsel at the National Center on Sexual Exploitation said face-recognition technology isn’t always accurate, and predators could potentially purchase verified accounts to continue to prey on children. Doing face verifications just once, she argues, gives predators “complete access to all the children on Roblox.”

“Roblox may be a virtual world, but the children are real,” James said during her testimony. “The predators are real. The addiction is real. The exploitation is real, and the consequences are real. Children should never have to enter a game marketed to them and wonder whether the person on the other side of the screen is there to play with them or prey on them.”

articleBody:
# Donald Trump: Technikprobleme in Serie – Kritik in eigenen Reihen wächst

Bild vergrößern Donald Trump (am 8. November)

Erst Microsoft . Dann die komplette Flugaufsicht. Und die Bank Chase. Jetzt auch noch Apple . Von der National Security Agency (NSA) ganz zu schweigen: Eine beispiellose Serie von Technik-Ausfällen hat in den USA Teile der Infrastruktur lahmgelegt. Während der Flugverkehr, Banken und Behörden seit Tagen mit massiven Störungen ​kämpfen, bemühte sich die US-Regierung, Sorgen vor einer tieferen Krise zu zerstreuen.

Präsident Donald Trump sagte am Rande eines Wirtschaftsgipfels in Manila : »So ist es halt im Leben. Wenn man groß und ‌mächtig ist und all das Geld hat, passierten solche Dinge.« Und weiter: »Das ist in Ordnung.«

Seine Worte stehen in scharfem Kontrast zu den weitreichenden Folgen der Pannen, die selbst bei Trumps Verbündeten den Ruf nach Aufklärung lauter werden lassen. »Wenn das alles ein Zufall ist, dann ist es der größte Zufall in der Weltgeschichte«, sagte etwa der republikanische US-Senator Josh Hawley.

Und auch aus dem engsten Kreis von Trumps Maga-Anhängern kommen kritische Töne. Der rechten Influencerin Laura Loomer wird eine große Nähe zu Trump nachgesagt. Sie erklärte nun: »Unsere Anführer belügen uns. Das ist eindeutig ein koordinierter Cyberangriff.« Belege lieferte sie nicht mit, offiziell wird ein Cyberangriff bisher bestritten.

> Our leaders are lying to us. This is very clearly a coordinated cyber attack. President Trump should come back to the United States. — Laura Loomer (@LauraLoomer) November 17, 2026

Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung.

Der ​Geheimdienst NSA hatte zuletzt erklärt, sein Netzwerk habe während routinemäßiger Wartungsarbeiten eine »vorübergehende Beeinträchtigung« erlitten. Die geschäftskritischen Fähigkeiten seien jedoch voll einsatzfähig geblieben.

- Reihe von Ausfällen: Internes Netzwerk von US-Geheimdienst NSA gestört 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Flugsicherheit in den USA: United Airlines meldet »großflächigen Systemausfall« – Hunderte Starts betroffen 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Stundenlange Störung: Microsoft erklärt Ausfall seiner Dienste mit monatealtem Programmierfehler 3 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 3 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
Am Freitag ⁠ein Ausfall bei ⁠der Flugsicherheitsbehörde FAA den US-Luftverkehr für viereinhalb Stunden zum Erliegen gebracht – der längste derartige Stopp seit den Anschlägen vom 11. September 2001. Über 10.000 Flüge fielen aus. Am Montag folgten Computerprobleme bei der Fluggesellschaft United Airlines sowie bei der Großbank JPMorgan . ‌Jüngst hatte bereits ein Ausfall bei Microsoft zahlreiche Dienste des Softwarekonzerns gestört.

### Führten Sparmaßnahmen zu den aktuellen Problemen?

Eine Sprecherin des ​Weißen Hauses sagte, Trump ‌habe Expertengruppen zusammengestellt, um die Probleme bei der FAA zu beheben. »Es gibt keine Krise oder ähnliches, worüber sich die Amerikaner Sorgen machen müssten«, sagte sie. Vizepräsident JD Vance sagte den Sender Fox News, er werde von Freunden gefragt, ob sie Bunker bauen oder Vorräte anlegen sollten. »Meine Antwort darauf ist nein, wir sehen keine Krise auf ‌uns zukommen, aber man muss auf alles vorbereitet sein.«

Experten weisen darauf hin, dass die Ausfälle bei vielen der betroffenen Organisationen auf massive Stellenstreichungen folgen. Bei der FAA hatte es nach Trumps Amtsantritt im vergangenen Jahr auf Betreiben ‌von Elon Musk erhebliche Kürzungen gegeben. Der Kongress hatte davor ​gewarnt, dass die beschleunigte Modernisierung der Behörde schlecht organisiert ‌sei und zu Ausfällen führen könnte.

- US-Präsident nach dem Sieg der Demokraten: »Ich werde Mr. Veto« – wie es für Trump jetzt weitergeht Eine Analyse von Marc Pitzke 5 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 5 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Treffen im Weißen Haus: Diese KI-Bosse waren Trump beim »Super Intelligence Luncheon« besonders nah Von Angela Gruber und Niklas Marienhagen 6 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 6 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- meinung meinung • Milliardärsideologie: Wenn Gier gut ist, sind die Gierigsten die Besten Eine Kolumne von Christian Stöcker 6 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 6 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
Auch Microsoft und United Airlines hatten zuletzt im ‌großen Stil Personal abgebaut, teils ​mit Verweis auf Effizienzgewinne durch Künstliche Intelligenz (KI). Zwar gibt es keine Beweise, dass die Entlassungen direkt zu den aktuellen Störungen geführt haben. Die Software-Expertin Liz Fong-Jones ​betonte jedoch, dass die Widerstandsfähigkeit von Systemen stark von erfahrenem Personal ⁠abhänge. Zugleich warnen Fachleute vor einer Zunahme von ​Cyberangriffen durch ​KI-Werkzeuge. Dem Versicherer Marsh zufolge meldeten Kunden in den letzten beiden Oktoberwochen 105 Cyber-Vorfälle – mehr als doppelt so viele wie Ende Mai.

articleBody:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new *"frontier* ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work."

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and [Clippy the assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Assistant) to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

Fiona, a hippopotamus who lives at the Cincinnati Zoo, became [a viral sensation](https://www.neatorama.com/pet/2017/04/04/Dreaming-Baby-Hippo-is-the-Cutest-Thing-Youll-See-Today/)when she was born prematurely in 2017. She was the smallest surviving hippo baby ever recorded. Fiona is still a zoo favorite, and that makes it all the more serious that she ate something she shouldn't have on Monday. Fiona swallowed a knit cap that got into her enclosure. You might think shame on anyone who throws objects into a zoo enclosure, but it's more complicated than that. The cap was tossed into the air by a visitor (like Mary Richards in *The Mary Tyler Moore Show* ) and was caught by a ceiling fan. The fan then catapulted the cap through a small opening above the zoo's viewing windows. It was a one-in-a-million shot. Ta da!

Fiona gobbled up the cap before zoo employees could retrieve it. Now she is being monitored by veterinarians [who are helping her to "pass the hat."](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/animal-news/cincinnati-zoo-says-fiona-hippo-undergoing-care-eating-hat-rcna609763)We're pulling for you, Fiona! -via [Fark](https://www.fark.com/comments/14265050/If-this-story-is-really-true-Ill-eat-my-wait-you-dont-say)

articleBody:
## jennifer latour assembles imaginary botanical creatures

Vancouver-based artist and photographer Jennifer Latour assembles [flowers](https://www.designboom.com/tag/flower-and-leaf-art/), stems, and other botanical fragments into unfamiliar sculptural forms in her ongoing series Bound Species and Shapeshifters. Drawing on her background in special effects makeup for film and television, she approaches each composition as a character, giving individual plants new shapes, proportions, and personalities.

*‘The overall composition has to speak to me, and I often see the pieces alive in my head. I visualize how it would speak and walk if it could. To me, each piece has their own distinct personality,’* **she [tells](https://www.designboom.com/tag/art-interviews/) designboom.**

Her interest in creating fictional forms goes back to childhood, when she was fascinated by moving shapes and objects. *‘I had hanging mobiles as a child and I remember the feeling of being captivated by moving shapes in daylight and seeing things morphing,’* **the artist recalls.**

Each composition is physically constructed and [photographed](https://www.designboom.com/tag/photography/), with its eventual appearance dependent on the behavior of the materials. Sometimes the flowers remain stable long enough for Latour to revisit and adjust a piece. More often, their gradual wilting determines when the work is complete. *‘It’s instinctual – I always run on feeling,’* **she says, explaining that the sculpture sometimes** *‘almost decides on its own.’*

Lough Gill, Ireland | all photography by Jennifer Latour

## assembling new species

Born in Seven Islands, Quebec, and now based in Vancouver, Jennifer Latour began experimenting with photography in 2006. Her practice took a new direction during the first COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, when she turned to still life and started experimenting with flowers. Bound Species grew from the idea of treating botanical elements as extensions of the body. By joining different plants, petals, stems, and buds, she began constructing unfamiliar organisms that suggest limbs, bodies, and other anatomical features.

The creative possibilities of this process are what continue to draw her in. *‘There’s something endless about it all and very exciting! I love the imagination I tap into when I start a new piece,’* **Jennifer Latour tells us.** For Latour, the compositions need to follow an internal logic of color and form, even when their final appearance belongs to an imagined world. She describes this as having *‘the vision that it could possibly exist somewhere on another planet.’*

Although the artist many times begins with a rough idea or drawing, the materials available at the time play a significant role in determining the final composition. Seasonal flowers introduce an element of unpredictability, requiring her to respond to their individual shapes and textures *. ‘When I get to a florist or garden center, I’m at the mercy of the season and the flora that stands out to me that’s available,’* **she explains.** From there, she begins joining and balancing the different elements, moving them around until the composition feels resolved. The process can take several hours, but the flowers’ short lifespan places a limit on how long she can work. When creating outdoors, wind can introduce another complication. *‘I’ve had countless pieces ready for the photo and just as I grab my camera everything falls apart!’* **the [artist](https://www.jenniferlatour.com/) shares.** *‘Patience and determination play a huge part in my practice!’*

Wild Specie no.35, Sun Peaks II

## from special effects makeup to botanical characters

Jennifer Latour’s background in special effects makeup has shaped the way she approaches her botanical work. Having spent years creating prosthetics and fictional creatures for film and television, she is accustomed to building characters through the combination of individual sculptural elements. The same thinking informs her approach to the plants, which she assembles into figures with their own imagined identities. *‘Creating characters through my sculptures is directly connected to how I approach a character in film,’* **she highlights.** She often visualizes the finished pieces as if they were alive, imagining how they might move or communicate. This character-driven perspective is particularly evident in Shapeshifters, where the botanical compositions take on more pronounced creature-like forms.

Her visual references span sculpture, photography, cinema, and animation. She cites Alexander Calder’s mobiles and Isamu Noguchi’s wood sculptures, alongside the photography of Tim Walker and the films of Wes Anderson and Tim Burton. Childhood memories also remain part of her visual vocabulary, including a pop-up edition of ‘The Wind in the Willows’ that she received as a child and became obsessed with. *‘Many more but the impact film, music and art have on me is an endless list,’* **Jennifer Latour adds.**

Wild Flower no.22, Cypress Mountain

## imagining an interconnected natural world

While each sculpture has its own character, the two series also consider the relationships between different forms of life. Latour sees the botanical figures as part of a wider reflection on how organisms are connected through both their similarities and differences. She hopes viewers will use the unfamiliar forms as a starting point for their own imagined worlds. *‘I hope they tap into their own imagination and can envision a world where the sculptures could exist,’* **she says.** *‘Everything is interconnected and we are all of us flora, creatures, humans, etc., both deeply bound together by our similarities and our differences.’*

articleBody:
# jQuery 4.1.0 and 3.8.0 Released: Passing the Torch | Official jQuery Blog

- Official jQuery Blog jQuery 4.1.0 and 3.8.0 Released: Passing the Torch Posted on November 17, 2026 by Timmy Willison jQuery 4.1.0 has arrived! And it brought a friend. Alongside the first minor release of the 4.x line, we're also releasing jQuery 3.8.0. A word of caution: 3.8.0 exists to release the fixes and improvements that have been pending on the 3.x-stable branch for the past few years, some of which you may recognize from the jQuery 4.0.0 release. It is a send-off, not a comeback. Going forward, the 3.x branch will only receive critical security and bug fixes. If you haven't yet made the jump to 4.x, we encourage you to do so — we have an upgrade guide and the jQuery Migrate plugin ready to help, and most users will be able to upgrade with minimal changes. As usual, the releases are available on our CDN and the npm package manager. Other third party CDNs will probably have them available soon as well, but remember that we don't control their release schedules and they will need some time. Here are the highlights. In both 4.1.0 and 3.8.0 A few changes landed on both branches, so you get these no matter which version you're on. A new API for AJAX transport complete callbacks Custom AJAX transports have long received a completeCallback with positional arguments: function( status, statusText, responses, headers ) {} Transports can now instead invoke the callback with a single object: function( { status, statusText, responses, headers } ) {} This makes it possible for us to add new parameters in the future without relying on their order, and for transports to provide them selectively. In fact, 4.1.0 already takes advantage of it — see responseURL below. Selector: ReDoS fix in identifier matching The regular expression jQuery uses to match identifiers in selectors was vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking; a long chain of hex escapes followed by an invalid character — for example, in an attribute selector — could hang the page. The production now explicitly excludes digits & hex characters where the spec says it should, bringing us closer to spec and eliminating the ReDoS. Selector: loose document comparisons everywhere IE & Edge Legacy sometimes throw on strict document comparisons ( === ) but not on loose ones ( == ). We switched most of these comparisons years ago, but a few leftovers remained in the selector code. They've now all been converted, avoiding some rare crashes in those browsers. What else is new in 4.1.0 jqXHR gains responseURL jqXHR objects now expose responseURL — the final URL of the request after any redirects followed by the browser. Following the existing responseText / responseXML / responseJSON pattern, it is only set when the transport can report it: modern-browser XHR provides it, while IE 11 and the script & JSONP transports do not. Serialize form-associated custom elements Form-associated custom elements — custom elements registered with formAssociated = true — now serialize correctly with .serialize() and .serializeArray() . Elements that appear in form.elements are trusted to be submittable rather than being filtered out by a tag name check. CSS methods work in XML documents In non-XHTML XML documents, such as XSLT-transformed documents, elements created with document.createElement land in the XML namespace and have no style property, which broke jQuery's CSS support tests. jQuery now uses createElementNS with the XHTML namespace internally, so .css() and friends behave in these documents. querySelectorAll everywhere jQuery no longer uses getElementsByTagName or getElementsByClassName internally, relying on querySelectorAll instead. In today's browsers, qSA is on par with or faster than the old methods, and returns a static list rather than a live collection that we had to snapshot. The switch also fixes some long-standing bugs, including MathML elements not being found by lowercase tag names on cloned nodes in IE 11, selectors with leading combinators not working on document fragments, and selection by tag names containing less common symbols such as dots. Related selector work makes the quick selection paths stricter about what counts as a simple tag or class selector — with a fallback to regular selection when qSA throws — and invalid escape sequences in selectors are now decoded to U+FFFD, the replacement character, as the CSS specification requires. Faster uniqueSort jQuery.uniqueSort removes duplicates with a single-pass, two-pointer compaction instead of repeated splices, taking the duplicate removal from O(N²) time and O(N) extra space to O(N) time and constant space. Behavior and ordering are unchanged; large disconnected sets just get there faster. What's in 3.8.0 Again, most of what's in 3.8.0 has been sitting on the branch for a while, and much of it will look familiar if you read the jQuery 4.0.0 release post . But there are a few things specific to 3.x. Support for hidden="until-found" The hidden attribute used to be a boolean attribute, but it has since gained the until-found value. jQuery 3.x normalized boolean attributes in a way that clobbered that value; .attr( "hidden", "until-found" ) now sets it as-is. jQuery 4.x changed how boolean attributes are handled precisely to avoid this class of problem, so no change was needed there. Deprecations to smooth the road to 4.x Two sets of APIs that were removed in jQuery 4.0.0 are now formally deprecated in 3.x, which means the jQuery Migrate plugin can warn you about them before you upgrade: The push , sort & splice Array methods on the jQuery prototype. These were always meant for internal use and jQuery itself hasn't used them since Sizzle was inlined. If you need the same behavior, $elems.push( elem ) can be replaced with [].push.call( $elems, elem ) .
- jQuery.expr[ ":" ] and jQuery.expr.filters , which have been documented as deprecated since 3.0.0 but never made their way into the deprecated module. Use jQuery.expr.pseudos instead.
### Backported fixes

3.8.0 also picks up a number of fixes that already shipped in jQuery 4.0.0, including support for self-removing scripts passed to .html() , a fix for jQuery.cleanData skipping elements during cleanup, correct dimensions for table <col> elements, more robust native event handling in leverageNative , and support test fixes for pages under CSS zoom and initially hidden iframes.

## Download

You can get the files from the jQuery CDN, or link to them directly:

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-4.1.0.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-4.1.0.min.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.8.0.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.8.0.min.js

You can also get this release from npm:

npm install jquery@4.1.0

npm install jquery@3.8.0

The slim builds are available as well:

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-4.1.0.slim.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-4.1.0.slim.min.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.8.0.slim.js

https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.8.0.slim.min.js

Information on all the ways to get jQuery is available at https://jquery.com/download/ .

One more time for the folks in the back: jQuery 3.8.0 is the last planned feature release on the 3.x branch. From here on, 3.x will only receive critical fixes. jQuery 4.x is where active development happens, and it's ready for you.

## Thanks

Thank you to all of you who participated in these releases by submitting patches, reporting bugs, or testing, including ac-mmi , Apoorv Darshan , Richard Gibson , Michał Gołębiowski-Owczarek , J.Son , Naveed Khan , metsw24-max , neogy-akash , orbisai0security , Stephen Sigwart , studystill , Timo Tijhof , TomTensor , 서울민트초코 , and the whole jQuery team.

## Changelogs

### 4.1.0

### Ajax

- Add the responseURL field to jqXHR ( #4339 , 5691e03a )
- Support an alternative completeCallback API for transports ( a05c3d73 )
### Core

- Refactor loops to avoid going behind array bounds ( 5f8ed054 )
- Drop getElementsBy{Tag,Class}Name in favor of querySelectorAll ( #3642 , 53a2bcf9 )
### CSS

- Empty the computeTableStyleTests probe table when it might be reused ( #5932 , f37226f0 )
- Use createElementNS to support XML documents ( #4730 , dcb31ae8 )
### Data

- Shave off some bytes ( eb9acfe9 )
### Docs

- Add a new commercial support vendor: TuxCare ( b75c1fef )
- Fix spelling of XMLHttpRequest in README (#5903) ( 71c0dd14 )
- Add guidelines for machine-generated contributions ( 51eb576c )
- Update the jQuery NES HeroDevs link in README (#5853) ( dd7b28f4 )
- Update active version table ( fef45254 )
- update README with 4.0 release ( #5781 , 5bffcc1a )
### Selector

- Work around a Safari 27 regex interepreter bug ( b557a8c4 )
- Fix the runescape regex in unescapeSelector ( e77f87c8 )
- Decode invalid escape code points to U+FFFD (#5845) ( 7e1efd77 )
- Optimize jQuery.uniqueSort duplicate removal ( 35789e76 )
- Be more strict in quick selection paths ( a104324d )
- Fix ReDoS in identifier matching ( d41cf7dd )
- Use loose document comparisons everywhere ( 74439453 )
### Serialize

- Support form-associated custom elements ( #5245 , 680c320c )
### 3.8.0

### Ajax

- Support an alternative completeCallback API for transports ( 43b8652b )
### Attributes

- Support the until-found value for the hidden attribute ( 85290c59 )
### Core

- Formally deprecate push/sort/splice ( 50d9a8dc )
- Simplify code post browser support reduction ( 6fe88690 )
### CSS

- Empty the computeTableStyleTests probe table when it might be reused (3.x) ( #5932 , 4bb01875 )
- Fix dimensions of table <col> elements ( #5628 , 3f70fbc7 )
- Tests: Fix tests & support tests under CSS Zoom (3.x version) ( #5489 , 29a9030c )
- Fix reliableTrDimensions test for initially hidden iframes (3.x) ( 4e989805 )
- Fix support test results for initially hidden iframes ( ac68b21f )
### Data

- Shave off some bytes ( 000feef3 )
### Docs

- Fix some minor issues in comments ( b57c4b51 )
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md ( d41f0cd9 )
- Update remaining HTTP URLs to HTTPS ( 5d5872bd )
### Event

- Increase robustness of an inner native event in leverageNative ( #5459 , 37bded35 )
### Manipulation

- Make jQuery.cleanData not skip elements during cleanup ( #5214 , 752e9119 )
- Generalize a test to support IE ( ab0444dd )
- Support $el.html(selfRemovingScript) ( #5377 , cbc15c9c )
### Selector

- Work around a Safari 27 regex interepreter bug ( 8df0f0d6 )
- Fix the runescape regex in unescapeSelector ( c4a98588 )
- Fix ReDoS in identifier matching ( dd23807d )
- Use loose document comparisons everywhere (3.x) ( 61bf6c6f )
- Properly deprecate jQuery.expr[ ":" ] / jQuery.expr.filters ( 5eab9df7 )
Comments are closed.

articleBody:
Many will recall **Erland Cooper**as the composer who buried the only copy of**[Carve the Runes Then Be Content With Silence](https://acloserlisten.com/2024/09/17/erland-cooper-carve-the-runes-then-be-content-with-silence)** in the ground, then challenged fans to find it, dig it up and return it. *Dawn Chorus* is a different beast, still in love with the great outdoors but noticeably above ground. Recorded with the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra featuring violinist Freya Goldmark, the set unfolds in four sumptuous suites, ending in notes as triumphant as the dawn.

When considering instrumental music, one rarely discusses earworms, although they do exist: the prominent attack of Beethoven’s Fifth, the lilting melody of “Für Elise,” and of course, “The Wedding March.” Cooper may have found his own in the six-note motif of “Paradisaea.” The composition rises from a series of quiet stringed passages, each falling into silence before rising again, giving way to the secondary and then the central theme. The composition imitates the slow blossoming of dawn, light peeking shyly over the horizon before announcing itself in full. A tender passage in the midst of the first movement indicates the fragility of the day before it has been established. Once that motif breaks through, so does the sun, and no amount of silence, no sonic shift can contain it.

Freya rises to a frenzy in the second movement, then relents, like a murmuration forming and dissipating. The third refreshes the motif, presenting it again in a round, by which point it has become lodged in the listener’s head. Drum rolls bring the piece to a rousing finale, waking the final residents of forest and field. “Erithacus rubecula” (“European Robin”) starts in far gentler fashion, with solo, exploratory notes, the single bird joined by the flock in the Allegretto. The dominant themes are wider, more expansive, like the light splayed across the countryside. The violin soars toward the heavens, outpacing the flock, unable to contain its excitement. The vast center of the Allegretto conjures images of prairies, unspoiled hopes and the splendour of a new day, while the third movement returns to the robin, undergirded by a gentle hum reflecting the warmth of the rising rays.

“Fratercula arctica” (“Atlantic Puffin”) is a surprisingly romantic composition. A series of lilting melodies leads to a swirl of orchestral activity, like a camera being drawn back to reveal an entire population. The second movement is calmer and more intimate, with hints of harp. Darker brass chords swoop in, revealing an unprecedented tension resolved by the early minutes of the Finale. This third movement is the album’s finest, earning its swoops of joy. The ending is so triumphant and seemingly definitive that on first play, one receives it as the end of the album and rises for an exuberant Bravo! ~ only to realize that there’s still one suite to come.

“Unfolding Landscapes” is a combination of encore, outlier and denouement. The shortest suite (unfolding in only two movements) and the only one to eschew Latin titles, the composition is also distinguished by the rhapsodic piano of “Pt. 1,” which leads to full orchestral accompaniment in “Pt. 2.” A quickening of pace leads to friendly staccato strings, which pause for a few regal seconds before racing to *Dawn Chorus’* s second, even grander finale. Drums join the fray, at first restrained and finally booming, a hummingbird tempo toppling into a bevy of brass. Two seconds of silence are followed by a 20-second cinematic peak. And now the album is *really* over, the sun erupting through the clouds, the earth rejoicing and every living creature giving praise. **(Richard Allen)**

articleBody:
The end of the year is quickly approaching, and you know what that means: gifting season is here.

Like clockwork, we’re back with a carefully curated, handy dandy [gift guide](https://colossal.shop/pages/2026-gift-guide) to help you pick out the perfect presents for each name on your list. Organized by passions and personalities, our list has something special for everyone. So sit back, brew a cup of tea, and get scrolling! You’re about to have the breeziest holiday shopping yet.

As always, thank you for supporting Colossal.

**For the Creative Professional**

Visual thinkers understand the absolute joy of [impeccably designed things](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-creative-professional). Treat the creative in your life to studio essentials that make the workday lighter and intriguing reads to keep the ideas flowing.

**For the Maximalist**

More is more! If bold colors, clashing patterns, and whimsical graphics are that special someone’s vibe, we’ve got the [perfect accessories](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-maximalist-1) to complete their closet.

**For the Nature Lover**

We all know someone who feels the happiest among flora, fauna, and the great outdoors. Bring [a bit of nature](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-nature-lover) to them with a new pair of gardening gloves, fungi-inspired decor and puzzles, a guide to foraging for handmade inks, and plenty more.

**For the Tasteful Host**

Those with great taste often have a cozy home to match. Help your favorite host make their space even warmer with [aesthetically-pleasing objects](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-tasteful-host) for cooking, gathering, and lingering just a bit longer.

**For the Serial Hobbyist**

Our exciting range of craft kits open up a world of possibilities for those who never seem to get tired of [trying new hobbies](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-serial-hobbyist). From hand loom weaving and embroidery to pressing flowers and growing herbs, there’s something new to try for everyone.

**For the Budding Artist**

What’s more important than encouraging those just beginning to explore their creative side? Surprise that [little one](https://colossal.shop/collections/for-the-budding-artist) with a big imagination with specially-crafted wooden toys, beautiful books, unique crayons, and beyond.

Find more in the [Colossal Shop](https://colossal.shop).

Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a [Colossal Member](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members) today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article [The Colossal Guide for Creative Gifting](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/11/colossal-gift-guide-2026/) appeared first on [Colossal](https://www.thisiscolossal.com).

title: Does video show Sean Duffy shifting stance on need for FAA funding from 2023 to 2026?
subtitle: The clip appears to show Duffy arguing the FAA needed "competent people" rather than more money in 2023 before asking for additional funding in 2026.

# Does video show Sean Duffy shifting stance on need for FAA funding from 2023 to 2026?

About this rating

Duffy said during a nationwide ground stop in January 2023 that the FAA needed competent people, not more funding. He was not transportation secretary at the time. More than three years later, in November 2026, he said his department needed more money during a nationwide ground stop that occurred on his watch.

In mid-November, a video montage spread purportedly showing U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy making contrasting statements about funding for the Federal Aviation Administration.

Some of the compilation's clips, said to be from 2023, supposedly show him saying the FAA needed more competent people, not more money, amid a nationwide ground stop that lasted less than two hours on Jan. 11 of that year. Duffy was not transportation secretary at that point. He appeared to be criticizing former President Joe Biden's administration.

Other parts of the video montage show Duffy nearly four years later, speaking as transportation secretary, requesting $50 billion in funding following the Nov. 13, 2026, outage that led to a nationwide grounding of flights lasting roughly five hours — the longest such stoppage since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

People shared versions of the compilation video on Facebook ( archived ), Instagram ( archived ), Reddit ( archived ) and TikTok . One Snopes reader asked, "Was Sean Duffy on Fox News Jan. 11, 2023, saying the FAA doesn't need more money but more competent people?"

To answer that reader's question, yes, the story is true. The clips in the video montage are real, meaning they were not created or manipulated with artificial intelligence tools.

Comedy Central's "The Daily Show" first posted the edited compilation video on Nov. 16 ( archived ).

A partial statement from the Transportation Department appears later in this article.

## Duffy's 2023 remarks

A search of the Internet Archive's TV News Archive website , which hosts historic footage of news programs, confirms that Duffy did say the remarks in the video montage that were said to be from 2023. On Jan. 11 of that year , he told Sandra Smith, the host of the Fox News show, "America Reports" (from the 2:36 mark onward):

> They got billions of dollars, the FAA did, over COVID. And now they're going to come back and say, "We want even more money to fix this crisis that we weren't able to handle when, you know, for what, three hours in the morning, aircraft couldn't fly." I don't know that it's more money, Sandra. I think it's just having competent people in leadership and throughout the building that can make the organization function, and you don't have that right now.

## Origin of November 2026 clips

The additional clips in "The Daily Show" video montage truly originate from recent broadcasts, as well. They show Duffy speaking about the grounding of flights in 2026.

During a Nov. 13 White House news conference regarding the ground stop, Duffy said, "I want $50 billion" ( 7:11 ), "Let's get the money" ( 7:51 ), and "I want $50 billion" ( 9:35 ). These clips appear between 0:13 and 0:16 in "The Daily Show" compilation video.

Other clips show Duffy saying, "I need additional money" ( 6:53 ) on "Fox News Sunday," "Congress can find a way to find the money" ( 5:27 ) and "All we need is the money" ( 7:57 ) on ABC News' "This Week With George Stephanopoulos," and "I need more money" ( 2:19 ) and "All I need is the money" ( 4:08 ) on NBC News' "Meet the Press." These clips appear between 0:20 and 0:26 in "The Daily Show" compilation video.

The final clip of Duffy confirming his $50 billion ask (from 0:26 onward in the video montage ) aired on CBS News' "Face the Nation" ( 9:25 ) on Nov. 15.

Snopes contacted the Transportation Department to ask if the comparison people were sharing is fair. A spokesperson responded by comparing Duffy's record to that of former Transportation Department Secretary Pete Buttigieg, who served under Biden during the January 2023 ground stop. That statement, criticizing Buttigieg, ended with, "Secretary Duffy pointed out the obvious: Buttigieg had no plan to fix the FAA. The Trump administration does."

For further reading, we previously examined whether Buttigieg's transportation department spent $80 billion on diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives while delaying air traffic control upgrades.

articleBody:
Does a video provide evidence that the United States is withdrawing troops from Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Syria and other Gulf countries in November 2026? No, that's not true: The video predates the conflict between the United States and Iran, which began on Feb. 28, 2026, and therefore cannot document withdrawals related to that conflict. Lead Stories found no matching reports from established news outlets confirming the claimed withdrawals of U.S. military personnel and assets from those countries.

The claim appeared in [a video](https://www.tiktok.com/@truthplugchannel/video/7707049822460595474) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261117213747/https://www.tiktok.com/@truthplugchannel/video/7707049822460595474) ) by the @truthplugchannel account on TikTok, uploaded on Nov. 11, 2026. The on-screen caption read:

> BREAKING NEWS Reports claim that the United States is withdrawing military personnel and assets from bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq, Jordan, the UAE, Syria, and other parts of the Gulf. 🇺🇸

This is what a screenshot of the video in the post looked like at the time of writing:

*(Image source: post by @truthplugchannel on TikTok.)*

The video is embedded below:

The caption to the post on TikTok read:

> 🚨 BREAKING: Reports claim that the United States is withdrawing military personnel and assets from bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq, Jordan, the UAE, Syria, and other parts of the Gulf. 🇺🇸
> Images circulating online are being presented as evidence of a major U.S. military pullback.
> 🇮🇷 Some are calling it a victory for Iran, but the scale and purpose of any reported withdrawals remain unclear.
> ⚠️ No complete U.S. withdrawal from these countries has been independently confirmed.

Note that although the video mentions reports claiming that the United States is withdrawing military personnel and assets from bases across the Gulf, the final line of the caption, which does not appear in the video itself, works as a disclaimer, saying: "No complete U.S. withdrawal from these countries has been independently confirmed."

articleBody:
# 51 Studien nachgerechnet: Anti-Aging-Pillen fallen bei der DNA-Uhr durch

(Bild: DC Studio / Shutterstock.com )

Medikamente senken den Wert der Altersuhr, Nahrungsergänzungsmittel kaum. Doch die Uhr selbst schwankt schon nach dem Mittagessen.

Drei Jahre jünger in acht Wochen: Das versprach 2021 eine kleine Studie aus den USA und landete prompt in den Schlagzeilen. Ein Team der Yale University wollte es genau wissen, rechnete nach und setzte elf zusätzliche epigenetische Uhren ein. Keine davon bestätigte den früheren Befund.

Die Analyse erschien im Fachmagazin Nature Medicine .

Die Gruppe um den Psychiater Albert Higgins-Chen sammelte für die Auswertung 51 Studien, in denen Menschen vor und nach einer Anti-Aging-Maßnahme Blut abgaben. Und auf alle wandten sie dieselben 16 üblichen Altersuhren an.

Das Ergebnis: Es sind nicht die vielen Nahrungsergänzungsmittel, die etwas bringen. Lediglich Medikamente und ein gesünderer Lebensstil senkten das gemessene Alter.

### Was die Uhr zählt

Grundlage der Altersmessung sind sogenannte epigenetische Uhren. Sie lesen kleine chemische Anhängsel an der DNA aus, die Methylgruppen. Deren Muster verschiebt sich im Lauf des Lebens, und bei der Auswertung schätzt ein Algorithmus daraus ein Alter in Jahren.

Im Jahr 2013 entdeckte der Altersforscher Steven Horvath diesen Mechanismus und daraus entwickelte er eines der ersten und bekanntesten Modelle. Aus dem DNA-Muster schätzten frühere Generationen an Forschern das kalendarische Alter und je näher das Ergebnis am tatsächlichen Alter lag, desto genauer galt das Modell. Wenn die Modelle ein biologisches Alter von 55 Jahren vorhersagten, obwohl die Person laut Kalender erst 50 war, so deuteten die Forscher das als schnelleres Altern. Und so kamen die Wissenschaftler auf das biologische Alter.

Das Problem an dem Modell war, dass es nur Stellen auf der DNA in den Blick nahm, die mit der Zeit mitlaufen. Für sie spielte es aber keine Rolle, wie gesund jemand lebte.

Neuere Modelle lernten, dies zu berücksichtigen, und so schafften es Modelle wie GrimAge oder DunedinPACE deutlich besser, Sterberisiko und das Tempo des Alterns vorherzusagen.

Die Yale-Forscher brachten es auf den Punkt: Die Uhren der ersten Generation spiegeln in erster Linie zufälliges Rauschen wider und reagierten kaum auf Eingriffe. Am deutlichsten schlugen DunedinPACE und eine überarbeitete GrimAge-Version aus.

### Pillen ohne Ausschlag

# 51 Studien nachgerechnet: Anti-Aging-Pillen fallen bei der DNA-Uhr durch

(Bild: DC Studio / Shutterstock.com )

Medikamente senken den Wert der Altersuhr, Nahrungsergänzungsmittel kaum. Doch die Uhr selbst schwankt schon nach dem Mittagessen.

Drei Jahre jünger in acht Wochen: Das versprach 2021 eine kleine Studie aus den USA und landete prompt in den Schlagzeilen. Ein Team der Yale University wollte es genau wissen, rechnete nach und setzte elf zusätzliche epigenetische Uhren ein. Keine davon bestätigte den früheren Befund.

Die Analyse erschien im Fachmagazin Nature Medicine .

Die Gruppe um den Psychiater Albert Higgins-Chen sammelte für die Auswertung 51 Studien, in denen Menschen vor und nach einer Anti-Aging-Maßnahme Blut abgaben. Und auf alle wandten sie dieselben 16 üblichen Altersuhren an.

Das Ergebnis: Es sind nicht die vielen Nahrungsergänzungsmittel, die etwas bringen. Lediglich Medikamente und ein gesünderer Lebensstil senkten das gemessene Alter.

### Was die Uhr zählt

Grundlage der Altersmessung sind sogenannte epigenetische Uhren. Sie lesen kleine chemische Anhängsel an der DNA aus, die Methylgruppen. Deren Muster verschiebt sich im Lauf des Lebens, und bei der Auswertung schätzt ein Algorithmus daraus ein Alter in Jahren.

Im Jahr 2013 entdeckte der Altersforscher Steven Horvath diesen Mechanismus und daraus entwickelte er eines der ersten und bekanntesten Modelle. Aus dem DNA-Muster schätzten frühere Generationen an Forschern das kalendarische Alter und je näher das Ergebnis am tatsächlichen Alter lag, desto genauer galt das Modell. Wenn die Modelle ein biologisches Alter von 55 Jahren vorhersagten, obwohl die Person laut Kalender erst 50 war, so deuteten die Forscher das als schnelleres Altern. Und so kamen die Wissenschaftler auf das biologische Alter.

Das Problem an dem Modell war, dass es nur Stellen auf der DNA in den Blick nahm, die mit der Zeit mitlaufen. Für sie spielte es aber keine Rolle, wie gesund jemand lebte.

Neuere Modelle lernten, dies zu berücksichtigen, und so schafften es Modelle wie GrimAge oder DunedinPACE deutlich besser, Sterberisiko und das Tempo des Alterns vorherzusagen.

Die Yale-Forscher brachten es auf den Punkt: Die Uhren der ersten Generation spiegeln in erster Linie zufälliges Rauschen wider und reagierten kaum auf Eingriffe. Am deutlichsten schlugen DunedinPACE und eine überarbeitete GrimAge-Version aus.

### Pillen ohne Ausschlag

Von den 51 untersuchten Maßnahmen senkten 19 das epigenetische Alter, fünf ließen es dagegen steigen. Bei 26 zeigte sich keine Wirkung. Nach strenger statistischer Korrektur blieben 13 senkende und drei steigende übrig.

Am stärksten wirkten Medikamente: Rheumamittel gegen den Entzündungsbotenstoff TNF und das Diabetesmittel Metformin schnitten am besten ab. Ernährung und Bewegung halfen ebenfalls, ihre Wirkung war aber deutlich schwächer.

Populäre Nahrungsergänzungsmittel blieben als Gruppe ohne messbaren Effekt. Entscheidend ist, was darunter fiel: unter anderem Omega-3-Fettsäuren, Folsäure mit Vitamin B12, Lavendelöl und Buchweizenextrakt.

Verkaufsschlager der Longevity-Szene wie NMN oder Resveratrol tauchen in der Liste der ausgewerteten Studien nicht auf. Die Aussage „Nahrungsergänzungsmittel wirken nicht“ gilt also nur bedingt.

Selbst bei den Medikamenten lohnt ein zweiter Blick, denn einen Effekt auf die Altersuhren hatten sie vor allem bei kranken Menschen. Zehn der 51 Studien liefen Menschen, die in Behandlung waren. Die übrigen 41 wurden mit gesunden Menschen durchgeführt – aber bei ihnen überstand kein Effekt die Korrektur für Mehrfachtests.

articleBody:
This privately funded, not-for-profit museum lets visitors witness the greatness and trials of the teams that made up the "Original Eight" of the Negro Leagues.

In a self guided tour explore the informative and interactive exhibits featuring the photos, artifacts and films that tell the stories of these baseball players and all the people that made these teams possible.

Notable highlights include:

The Exhibition Gallery Film entitled "They Were All Stars" with narration by the acclaimed James Earl Jones. This film is a museum exclusive.

A timeline of baseball and African American history along with one-of-a-kind photographs, artifacts and stories to better envision the legacies told!

The Field of Legends that allows you to step into history with a stunning recreation of a baseball diamond, featuring bronze statues of all the greatest League players in their starring positions.

title: Computer Simulations Provide the Best Explanation for Those "Little Red Dots" Yet!
subtitle: Tiny ‘Little Red Dot’ galaxies found by the James Webb Space Telescope are revealed to be the remnants of supermassive primordial stars surrounded by dense gaseous envelopes.
feedText: Tiny ‘Little Red Dot’ galaxies found by the James Webb Space Telescope are revealed to be the remnants of supermassive primordial stars surrounded by dense gaseous envelopes.
articleBody:
# Computer Simulations Provide the Best Explanation for Those "Little Red Dots" Yet!

When the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) made its famous observations of several deep fields in the cosmos, astronomers were surprised to see numerous galaxies that defied expectations. These galaxies were bright and red - earning them the nickname Little Red Dots (LRDs) - and far more abundant than cosmological models predicted. Scientists theorized that these were early quasars, galaxies with active galactic nuclei (AGNs) powered by the "seeds" that would grow to become supermassive black holes (SMBHs).

However, this also conflicted with cosmological models, as it seemed unlikely that many galaxies could have formed with massive black holes less than one billion years after the Big Bang. This led scientists to consider various theories, compact collections of stars , "dusty" galaxies, supermassive stars, and "black hole stars." While the more recent Direct Collapse Black Holes (DCBHs) theory offered the most compelling argument to date, new simulations by an international team of astronomers indicate that they may be the remnants of collapsed supermassive primordial stars .

The study was led by Dr. Daniel Whalen from the University of Portsmouth's Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation . His colleagues included researchers from United Arab Emirates University , the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki , the Institute for Astronomy and Royal Observatory at the University of Edinburgh, and the Harvard & Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (CfA). The paper detailing their findings was published in the The Astrophysical Journal Letters .

The little red dots could represent galaxies in an evolutionary phase predating the luminous quasar phase. Credit: NASA/ESA/CSA/ISTA)/ETH Zurich/NAOJ

Previous attempts to explain the rapid formation, abundance, and spectral characteristics of LRDs all suffered from the same issue. While each explained some characteristics, none could account for everything the JWST revealed in its deep field surveys. Then came the DCBHs theory, which argues that SMBH seeds formed directly from massive clouds of cold gas. While this theory did fit Webb's observations nicely, it still faces numerous theoretical and environmental challenges.

For starters, the core premise of the DCBH theory is that a massive cloud of cold gas could collapse under its own gravity. However, gas tends to fragment into smaller clouds as it cools, leading to a cluster of primordial (Population III) stars instead of a black hole seed. To prevent fragmentation, the gas cloud must remain hot, requiring a very specific amount of Lyman-Werner (LW) radiation from a synchronized star-forming galaxy in its vicinity to destroy the main coolant - i.e., molecular hydrogen (H₂).

This raises additional problems, including the self-shielding nature of molecular hydrogen. As a gas cloud becomes increasingly dense, its outer layers absorb the LW radiation, shielding the inner core. This means that the critical amount of radiation required to suppress cooling across the entire cloud would be much higher. Even if the SMBH seed did manage to form, the radiative pressure it would emit (plus mechanical feedback from the disk and jets) would slow the accretion rate, significantly slowing further growth.

Whalen and his team found another explanation borne out by advanced cosmological simulations. As he said in a University of Portsmouth press release :

> LRDs have been one of the most surprising discoveries made by the James Webb Space Telescope. They are compact, only a few hundred light-years across, but are as bright as much larger galaxies, and their unusual V-shaped spectra have defied the usual astrophysical explanations. Their lack of detectable X-ray and radio emissions has left astronomers struggling to explain what they are.

Artist's impression of a galaxy forming stars within powerful outflows of material blasted out from supermassive black holes at its core. Credit: ESO/M. Kornmesser

Based on their simulations, the team produced a model showing that LRDs are most likely galaxies with AGN powered by massive black holes that formed through the collapse of supermassive primordial stars. What's more, their model suggests that the black holes are largely concealed by dense, massive discs of the gas that created them. These gaseous envelopes trap high-energy X-rays while allowing some visible, ultraviolet, and infrared light to escape, which fits with the unusual light signatures detected by the JWST.

The simulations also explain another long-standing mystery about LRDs: that a large cluster of stars in the disks of these small galaxies produces the blue part of the spectrum Webb observed. These disks, according to the models, contain around 100 million stars densely packed into regions measuring only 500 light-years in diameter, matching what astronomers observed in LRDs. Based on the available data, the team further concludes the black holes at the center of these primordial galaxies are only about 10 million Solar masses.

This is a few orders of magnitude less than previous estimates, which indicated a maximum of 100 million Solar masses. While this research is unlikely to be the final word on the nature of LRDs, it offers what is (to date) the most fitting explanation that matches the observations. "What makes this discovery so exciting is that we may be witnessing the birth of the first supermassive black holes," said Whalen. "For decades, simulations have predicted that these objects should exist, and now the James Webb Space Telescope may finally be allowing us to see them."

Further Reading: University of Portsmouth , The Astrophysical Journal Letters

### Matthew Williams

Matt Williams is a space journalist, science communicator, and author with several published titles and studies. His work is featured in The Ross 248 Project and Interstellar Travel edited by NASA alumni Les Johnson and Ken Roy. He also hosts the podcast series Stories from Space on Patreon. He lives in beautiful British Columbia with his wife and family. For more information, check out his website .

# Chip-Konzern: Nvidia verdoppelt erneut Umsatz und Gewinn – keine Pläne für Rückkehr Huangs

Nvidia: Es ist der ersten Quartalsbericht ohne Jensen Huang. Foto: REUTERS San Francisco, Frankfurt. Es war eine besondere Quartalskonferenz. Bisher waren Nvidias Analystenschalten zur Vorlage der Zahlen vor allem eines: eine Bühne für Gründer und CEO Jensen Huang. Routiniert und jovial führte er durch die Bilanz, schließlich gab es in den vergangenen Jahren meist nur Rekorde zu berichten. Ähnlich freundlich waren die meisten Analysten, die dem „KI-Papst“ mit harmlosen Fragen schmeichelten. Am Dienstag war alles anders.

Das ging mit dem Mann los, der die Analystenkonferenz eröffnete: Harvey Jones, der frisch ernannte Vorsitzende des Nvidia-Verwaltungsrats – ein Posten, den es bislang gar nicht gab. Ein wenig war sie Jones anzumerken, die Anspannung, die der seit der Gründung vor 33 Jahren im Aufsichtsgremium vertretene Wagniskapitalinvestor verspüren musste. Doch in seinen Aussagen war Jones glasklar.

Huang sei „nach der Offenlegung eines persönlichen Verhaltens, das im Widerspruch zum Verhaltenskodex, den Standards und den kulturellen Normen des Unternehmens stand, von seinen Ämtern“ zurückgetreten, sagte Jones. „Der Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat hat seinen Rücktritt einstimmig angenommen und beabsichtigt nicht, Jensen wieder als CEO einzusetzen.“

articleBody:
I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine.

I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects.

My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations:

external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly.

external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance.

external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package!

Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code.

The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running:

I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. This external sandbox pattern provides a neat way to experiment with different approaches.

subtitle: Comet Sound’s free OR-70 plugin combines eight effect modules, including spectral, granular, half-speed and pitch-shifting processing, under a single MORPH control for creating layered textures fro…
feedText: Comet Sound’s free OR-70 plugin combines eight effect modules, including spectral, granular, half-speed and pitch-shifting processing, under a single MORPH control for creating layered textures from existing audio.… Read More Comet Sound Intros Free OR-70 Morphing Effects Processor For Mac, Windows
articleBody:
# Comet Sound Intros Free OR-70 Morphing Effects Processor For Mac, Windows

Comet Sound has released OR-70 , a free multi-effects plugin designed to transform existing audio into layered textures using a combination of spectral, granular, rhythmic and harmonic processing.

The plugin is built around a single MORPH control that blends the original signal with the processed layers.

OR-70 is designed to work with source material such as synthesizer pads, vocals and audio loops. Its eight processing modules combine several types of sound manipulation, with the central MORPH control coordinating multiple parameters as the effect develops.

Features:

- Eight processing modules: GHOST, GRAIN, HALF, DRIVE, CHORUS, FLANGE, ORBIT and SHIFT.
- GHOST creates a spectral layer derived from the original audio.
- GRAIN adds granular processing, with density adjustable from smooth to granular textures.
- HALF provides half-speed playback synchronized to the bar.
- DRIVE adds saturation with tone control.
- ORBIT creates tempo-synchronized echoes, while SHIFT adds semitone transposition and shimmer.
- CHORUS and FLANGE provide additional modulation effects.
- MORPH controls density, blur, feedback and shimmer together, moving between the original source and the processed result.
- FREEZE captures the current effect state, while HOLD sustains it for as long as the control is pressed.
- MUTATE generates variations of the internal processing, with A/B comparison and BYPASS controls.
- 48 factory presets organized into eight categories: Texture, Wide, Dark, Rhythm, Dream, Glitch, Cinema and Vocal.
Pricing & Availability:

Comet Sound OR-70 is available as a free download from the Comet Sound website . The developer says the plugin requires no license key, trial activation or subscription, and has no time limit.
